title.raw: 卷九十八 元后傳 Volume 98: Wang Zhengjun

sentences.zh: 卷九十八 元后傳第六十八

translations.literal: Volume 98, Biography of the Empress Yuan the Sixth of Sixty-Eight
translations.idiomatic: Volume 98: Biography of Empress Yuan, number sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 孝元皇后，王莽姑也。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoyuan was the aunt of Wang Mang.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Xiaoyuan was Wang Mang's paternal aunt.

sentences.zh: 莽自謂黃帝之後，其《自本》曰：黃帝姓姚氏，八世生虞舜。

translations.literal: Mang claimed descent from the Yellow Emperor; his "Record of His Own Origin" says: The Yellow Emperor bore the surname Yao, and in the eighth generation there was Shun of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang styled himself a descendant of the Yellow Emperor; in his own genealogical memoir he wrote that the Yellow Emperor's clan name was Yao and that eight generations later came Shun of Yu.

sentences.zh: 舜起媯汭，以媯為姓。

translations.literal: Shun rose at the bend of the Gui and took Gui as his surname.
translations.idiomatic: Shun rose to power from the banks of the Gui and adopted Gui as his surname.

sentences.zh: 至周武王封舜後媯滿於陳，是為胡公，十三世生完。

translations.literal: When King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed Shun's descendant Gui Man in Chen, this was Duke Hu; in the thirteenth generation Man's line produced Wan.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed Shun's descendant Gui Man in Chen as Duke Hu; thirteen generations later the line reached Wan.

sentences.zh: 完字敬仲，奔齊，齊桓公以為卿，姓田氏。

translations.literal: Wan's style name was Jingzhong; he fled to Qi, Duke Huan of Qi made him a minister, and his surname became Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, whose courtesy name was Jingzhong, fled to Qi; Duke Huan of Qi appointed him minister, and the family took the surname Tian.

sentences.zh: 十一世，田和有齊國，二世稱王，至王建為秦所滅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh generation Tian He seized the state of Qi; for two generations they called themselves kings, until King Jian was destroyed by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven generations on, Tian He took control of Qi; two generations of his house assumed the royal title before King Jian was extinguished by Qin.

sentences.zh: 項羽起，封建孫安為濟北王。

translations.literal: When Xiang Yu rose, he enfeoffed Jian's grandson An as king of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Yu rose in rebellion, he made Jian's grandson An king of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 至漢興，安失國，齊人謂之「王家」，因以為氏。

translations.literal: When Han arose, An lost his state; the people of Qi called them the "king's household" and they therefore took that as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: After the Han rose, An lost his kingdom; the people of Qi spoke of the family as the "royal house," and from that they took the surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 文、景間，安孫遂字伯紀，處東平陵，生賀，字翁孺。

translations.literal: Between the reigns of Wendi and Jingdi, An's grandson Sui, style name Boji, lived at Dongpingling and fathered He, style name Wengru.
translations.idiomatic: In the time between Emperors Wen and Jing, An's grandson Wang Sui, courtesy name Boji, lived at Dongpingling and had a son named He, courtesy name Wengru.

sentences.zh: 為武帝繡衣御史，逐捕魏郡群盜堅盧等黨與，及吏畏懦逗留當坐者，翁孺皆縱不誅。

translations.literal: As embroidered-gown censor for Emperor Wu he pursued and captured the confederates of the bandit Jian Lu and others in Wei commandery, and also officials who out of cowardice had stalled and deserved punishment; Wengru released them all and did not execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as the emperor's embroidered-gown censor, he ran down the associates of the Wei bandit Jian Lu and the like, together with timid officials who had dragged their feet and merited death for it; Wang Wengru set every one of them free.

sentences.zh: 它部御史暴勝之等奏殺二千石，誅千石以下，及通行飲食坐連及者，大部至斬萬餘人，語見《酷吏傳》。

translations.literal: Censors in other sections such as Bao Shengzhi memorialized to execute two-thousand-bushel officials and put to death those below one thousand bushels, and those implicated merely for having given them food or drink on the road; in the largest cases they cut off more than ten thousand heads, as related in the "Biographies of the Harsh Officials."
translations.idiomatic: Other censors, Bao Shengzhi among them, asked leave to kill two-thousand-bushel officials and everyone down to the thousand-bushel rank, and anyone caught merely for having fed or lodged them; the biggest sweeps took more than ten thousand lives, as told in the "Harsh Officials" chapter.

sentences.zh: 翁孺以奉使不稱免，歎曰：「吾聞活千人者有封子孫，吾所活者萬餘人，後世其興乎！」

translations.literal: Wengru was dismissed for unsatisfactory performance of his mission and sighed: "I have heard that whoever saves a thousand lives will have descendants ennobled; I have kept more than ten thousand alive—will posterity not rise on my account?"
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed for failing in his assignment, he sighed: "They say saving a thousand men wins a fief for one's heirs. I spared well over ten thousand—perhaps fortune awaits my line after all."

sentences.zh: 翁孺既免，而與東平陵終氏為怨，乃徙魏郡元城委粟里，為三老，魏郡人德之。

translations.literal: After Wengru was dismissed he fell out with the Zhong family of Dongpingling and therefore moved to Weisui Lane in Yuancheng in Wei commandery, where he became a village elder, and the people of Wei were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once dismissed, he made an enemy of the Zhong clan of Dongpingling and moved to Weisui Lane in Yuancheng, Wei commandery, serving as a village elder whom the locals came to esteem.

sentences.zh: 元城建公曰：「昔春秋沙麓崩，晉史卜之，曰：『陰為陽雄，土火相乘，故有沙麓崩。

translations.literal: The village elder Jian of Yuancheng said: "In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when Shalu collapsed, the historian of Jin divined about it and said: 'Yin is the male of yang; earth and fire press upon each other—therefore Shalu collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: An elder of Yuancheng named Jian said: "When Shalu fell in the Spring and Autumn period, Jin's scribes divined and said, 'Yin contends as the male partner of yang; earth and fire grind against each other—hence the landslide at Shalu.

sentences.zh: 後六百四十五年，宜有聖女興。

translations.literal: In six hundred forty-five years thereafter, a holy woman ought to arise.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred forty-five years later a sage woman should arise.

sentences.zh: 』其齊田乎！

translations.literal: Is it not to be in Qi, among the Tian?'
translations.idiomatic: Will it not be among the Tian of Qi?"

sentences.zh: 今王翁孺徙，正真其地，日月當之。

translations.literal: Now Wang Wengru has moved here, precisely to this very place, where sun and moon converge.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wang Wengru has settled exactly on that ground, under the conjunction of sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 元城郭東有五鹿之虛，即沙鹿地也。

translations.literal: East of the wall of Yuancheng lies the waste of Five Deer—that is the ground of Shalu.
translations.idiomatic: East of Yuancheng's wall lies the barren tract called Five Deer—the old site of Shalu.

sentences.zh: 後八十年，當有貴女興天下」云。

translations.literal: In eighty years more, a noble woman will arise and rule the realm," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In another eighty years a woman of high destiny will rise to sway the realm," people said.

sentences.zh: 翁孺生禁，字稚君，少學法律長安，為廷尉史，本始三年，生女政君，即元后也。

translations.literal: Wengru fathered Jin, style name Zhijun, who in youth studied law in Chang'an and became a clerk of the commandant of justice; in the third year of Benshi he had a daughter, Zhengjun, who became Empress Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He begat Wang Jin, courtesy name Zhijun, who studied law in Chang'an as a young man and served as a clerk under the commandant of justice; in the third year of Benshi (71 BCE) his daughter Zhengjun was born—she who would become Empress Yuan.

sentences.zh: 禁有大志，不修廉隅，好酒色，多取傍妻，凡有四女八男；

translations.literal: Jin had great ambitions, did not fuss over petty integrity, loved wine and women, and took many secondary wives; in all he had four daughters and eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin nursed large designs, cared little for small scruples, and indulged in wine and concubines; he fathered four daughters and eight sons.

sentences.zh: 長女君俠，次即元后政君，次君力，次君弟；

translations.literal: The eldest daughter was Junxia; next came Empress Yuan, Zhengjun; then Junli; then Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest daughter was Junxia; next came Zhengjun, the future empress; then Junli and Junyi.

sentences.zh: 長男鳳孝卿，次曼元卿，譚子元，崇少子，商子夏，立子叔，根稚卿，逢時委卿，唯鳳、崇與元后政君同母。

translations.literal: The eldest son was Feng, courtesy name Xiaoqing; next Man, courtesy name Yuanqing; Tan, courtesy name Ziyuan; Chong, courtesy name Shaozi; Shang, courtesy name Zixia; Li, courtesy name Shuzi; Gen, courtesy name Zhijun; Fengshi, courtesy name Weiqing; only Feng and Chong shared the same mother as Empress Yuan, Zhengjun.
translations.idiomatic: The sons were, in order, Feng (Xiaoqing), Man (Yuanqing), Tan (Ziyuan), Chong (Shaozi), Shang (Zixia), Li (Shuzi), Gen (Zhijun), and Fengshi (Weiqing); only Feng and Chong were born of the same mother as Zhengjun.

sentences.zh: 母，適妻，魏郡李氏女也。

translations.literal: Their mother, his principal wife, was a daughter of the Li family of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother was his legitimate wife, a woman of the Li clan of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 後以妒去，更嫁為河內苟賓妻。

translations.literal: Later, out of jealousy, she was sent away and remarried as wife to Gou Bin of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Later he divorced her for jealousy; she married again as the wife of Gou Bin of Henei.

sentences.zh: 初，李親任政君在身，夢月入其懷。

translations.literal: At first, while Li was pregnant with Zhengjun, she dreamed that the moon entered her bosom.
translations.idiomatic: While Li was still carrying Zhengjun, she dreamed the moon slipped into her womb.

sentences.zh: 及壯大，婉順得婦人道。

translations.literal: When she grew up, she was gentle and compliant and behaved as a wife ought.
translations.idiomatic: As she grew, she was mild and yielding in the way expected of a woman.

sentences.zh: 嘗許嫁，未行，所許者死。

translations.literal: Once she was betrothed, but before the wedding her intended died.
translations.idiomatic: She was promised in marriage once, but before the ceremony could take place the bridegroom died.

sentences.zh: 後東平王聘政君為姬，未入，王薨。

translations.literal: Later the king of Dongping took her as a concubine, but before she entered the palace the king died.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Dongping then chose her as a concubine; before she could enter his household the prince died.

sentences.zh: 禁獨怪之，使卜數者相政君：「當大貴，不可言。

translations.literal: Jin alone thought it strange and sent diviners to read Zhengjun's fate: "She will reach the highest eminence; it cannot be put into words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin alone found this uncanny and had fortune-tellers examine her face: "She is destined for supreme rank—beyond what words can tell.

sentences.zh: 」禁心以為然，乃教書，學鼓琴。

translations.literal: " Jin took this to be true and had her taught writing and the zither.
translations.idiomatic: He believed them and had her taught letters and the zither.

sentences.zh: 五鳳中，獻政君，年十八矣，入掖庭為家人子。

translations.literal: In the Wufeng era he presented Zhengjun; she was eighteen when she entered the Yeeting as a family attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Wufeng he offered her at court; at eighteen she entered the imperial women's quarters as a family attendant.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，會皇太子所愛幸司馬良娣病，且死，謂太子曰：「妾死非天命，乃諸娣妾良人更祝詛殺我。

translations.literal: After more than a year it happened that Sima, the good-conduct maid favored by the heir apparent, fell ill and, as she was dying, said to the heir: "My death is not heaven's decree; the other concubines and good people have cursed me to death by turns.
translations.idiomatic: A year or so later the heir's beloved attendant, the Sima good-conduct maid, sickened and, dying, told him, "I am not dying of natural fate—the other concubines have taken turns cursing me to death.

sentences.zh: 」太子憐之，且以為然。

translations.literal: " The heir pitied her and believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The heir mourned her and believed her.

sentences.zh: 及司馬良娣死，太子悲恚發病，忽忽不樂，因以過怒諸娣妾，莫得進見者。

translations.literal: When Sima died, the heir was stricken with grief and rage and fell ill; he grew dull and joyless and therefore vented his anger on the concubines, and none could gain audience.
translations.idiomatic: After she died he sank into grief and rage, fell ill, and moped in misery, then turned his fury on every concubine and shut them all out.

sentences.zh: 久之，宣帝聞太子恨過諸娣妾，欲順適其意，乃令皇后擇後宮家人子可以虞侍太子者，政君與在其中。

translations.literal: After a long while Xuandi heard that the heir blamed his concubines excessively and wished to suit his mind; he ordered the empress to pick family attendants from the rear palace who might wait on the heir, and Zhengjun was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In time Emperor Xuan learned the heir was tormenting his women and meant to ease his temper; he told the empress to select family attendants from the harem to serve the heir, and Zhengjun was on the list.

sentences.zh: 及太子朝，皇后乃見政君等五人，微令旁長御問知太子所欲。

translations.literal: When the heir came to court, the empress showed Zhengjun and four others to him and quietly had a senior attendant at her side ask whom the heir desired.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir came to audience, the empress presented Zhengjun and four others and quietly had a senior woman-in-waiting learn which he favored.

sentences.zh: 太子殊無意於五人者，不得已於皇后，強應曰：「此中一人可。

translations.literal: The heir had no real interest in any of the five; constrained by the empress, he answered reluctantly, "One among these will do.
translations.idiomatic: He cared nothing for any of the five; pressed by the empress he muttered that one of them would do.

sentences.zh: 」是時政君坐近太子，又獨衣絳緣諸于，長御即以為是。

translations.literal: " At that moment Zhengjun sat nearest the heir and alone wore a jacket with a deep-red border; the senior attendant took her to be the one.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengjun happened to sit closest to him and was the only one in a jacket piped with crimson; the attendant assumed she was his choice.

sentences.zh: 皇后使侍中杜輔、掖庭令濁賢交送政君太子宮，見丙殿。

translations.literal: The empress ordered Palace Attendant Du Fu and Yeeting Director Zhuo Xian to escort Zhengjun together to the heir's palace, to Bing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The empress sent Palace Attendant Du Fu and Yeeting Director Zhuo Xian to conduct Zhengjun to the heir's residence and the Bing Hall.

sentences.zh: 得御幸，有身。

translations.literal: She received his favor and conceived.
translations.idiomatic: He lay with her once, and she conceived.

sentences.zh: 先是者，太子後宮娣妾以十數，御幸久者七八年，莫有子，及王妃一幸而有身。

translations.literal: Before this, the heir's rear palace had numbered in the tens of concubines; those favored longest had gone seven or eight years without bearing a child, yet the royal consort conceived after a single visit.
translations.idiomatic: Until then dozens of concubines had shared his bed, some favored seven or eight years, yet none had conceived; the royal consort conceived from that one union.

sentences.zh: 甘露三年，生成帝於甲館畫堂，為世適皇孫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Ganlu she bore Emperor Cheng at the painted hall of the Jia lodge, the first legitimate imperial grandson of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Ganlu (51 BCE) she bore Emperor Cheng in the painted hall of the Jia lodge—the generation's legitimate heir in the direct line.

sentences.zh: 宣帝愛之，自名曰驁，字太孫，常置左右。

translations.literal: Xuandi loved the child, himself gave him the personal name Ao and the style Taisun, and kept him constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan doted on the boy, personally named him Ao with the style Taisun, and kept him always near.

sentences.zh: 後三年，宣帝崩，太子即位，是為孝元帝。
立太孫為太子，以母王妃為婕妤，封父禁為陽平侯。
後三日，婕妤立為皇后，禁位特進，禁弟弘至長樂衛尉。
永光二年，禁薨，謚曰頃侯。
長子鳳嗣侯，為衛尉侍中，皇后自有子後，希復進見。
太子壯大，寬博恭慎，語在《成紀》。
其後幸酒，樂燕樂，元帝不以為能。
而傅昭儀有寵於上，生定陶共王。
王多材藝，上甚愛之，坐則側席，行則同輦，常有意欲廢太子而立共王。
時鳳在位，與皇后、太子同心憂懼，刺侍中史丹擁右太子，語在《丹傳》。
上亦以皇后素謹慎，而太子先帝所常留意，故得不廢。
元帝崩，太子立，是為孝成帝。

translations.literal: When Yuandi died, the heir ascended as Emperor Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan died, the heir mounted the throne as Emperor Cheng.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后為皇太后，以鳳為大司馬大將軍領尚書事，益封五千戶。

translations.literal: They honored the empress as empress dowager, appointed Feng grand marshal and general-in-chief with charge of the Masters of Writing, and added five thousand households to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was elevated to empress dowager; Wang Feng was made grand marshal and general-in-chief with oversight of the Masters of Writing, with an extra five thousand households added to his enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 王氏之興自鳳始。

translations.literal: The rise of the Wang began with Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The ascendancy of the Wang clan began with Wang Feng.

sentences.zh: 又封太后同母弟崇為安成侯，食邑萬戶。

translations.literal: They also enfeoffed the empress dowager's younger uterine brother Chong as marquis of Ancheng with revenue from ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Her uterine brother Chong was also enfeoffed as marquis of Ancheng with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 鳳庶弟譚等皆賜爵關內侯，食邑。

translations.literal: Feng's younger brothers by secondary wives, Tan and the rest, were all given noble rank as full marquises within the passes, with revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's half-brothers Tan and the others were all granted rank as secondary marquises within the passes, each with a stipend.

sentences.zh: 其夏，黃霧四塞終日。

translations.literal: That summer yellow fog filled the four quarters all day long.
translations.idiomatic: That summer a yellow mist blanketed the realm from horizon to horizon.

sentences.zh: 天子以問諫大夫楊興、博王駟勝等，對皆以為：「陰盛侵陽之氣也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven asked Remonstrance Grandee Yang Xing, Erudite Wang Sisheng, and others; they all replied that it was the qi of yin encroaching on yang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put the matter to Remonstrance Grandee Yang Xing, Erudite Wang Sisheng, and others; they agreed it was the vapor of yin pressing upon yang.

sentences.zh: 高祖之約也，非功臣不侯，今太后諸弟皆以無功為侯，非高祖之約，外戚未曾有也，故天為見異。

translations.literal: Gaozu's covenant was that none who were not merit officials should be marquises; now the empress dowager's brothers have all been made marquises without merit—not Gaozu's rule—and such a thing had never happened with affinal kin before; therefore heaven showed this anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: The founder's pact said only men of proven merit might hold a marquisate; now the empress dowager's brothers are all ennobled without merit—contrary to that pact and without precedent among in-laws—so heaven has sent this portent.

sentences.zh: 」言事者多以為然。

translations.literal: Those who spoke on policy mostly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Most who addressed the court thought them right.

sentences.zh: 鳳於是懼，上書辭謝曰：「陛下即位，思慕諒闇，故詔臣鳳典領尚書事，上無以明聖德，下無以益政治。

translations.literal: Feng therefore grew afraid and submitted a memorial declining responsibility, saying: "Since Your Majesty's accession you have mourned in the dark palace, therefore you ordered your servant Feng to take charge of the Masters of Writing; above I have not clarified sagely virtue, below I have not improved governance.
translations.idiomatic: Feng grew frightened and memorialized a self-rebuke: "Since you took the throne you have kept mourning seclusion, so you bade me Feng oversee the Masters of Writing; yet I have done nothing aloft to display your sage virtue or below to better the administration.

sentences.zh: 今有孛星天地赤黃之異，咎在臣鳳，當伏顯戮，以謝天下。

translations.literal: Now there is a broom star and anomalies of heaven and earth turning crimson-yellow; the fault lies with your servant Feng; I ought to suffer public execution to apologize to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Now a comet has appeared and heaven and earth have flushed red-yellow—the blame is mine; I deserve public execution to answer to the empire.

sentences.zh: 今諒闇已畢，大義皆舉，宜躬親萬機，以承天心。

translations.literal: Now the mourning seclusion is finished and the great rites have all been performed; you ought personally to handle the myriad affairs and answer heaven's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Your mourning is ended and the chief ceremonies done; you should take the myriad threads of government into your own hands and respond to heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 」因乞骸骨辭職。

translations.literal: " He therefore begged to surrender his bones and resign his office.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to retire and yield his post.

sentences.zh: 上報曰：「朕承先帝聖緒，涉道未深，不明事情，是以陰陽錯繆，日月無光，赤黃之氣，充塞天下。

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "I inherit the sage thread of the former emperors; I have not gone far along the Way and do not understand how things stand, so yin and yang are in disorder, sun and moon lack light, and crimson-yellow qi fills the world.
translations.idiomatic: The reply ran: "I continue the sacred line of my predecessors; my grasp of the Way is shallow and I misread affairs, so yin and yang tangle, sun and moon lose their radiance, and a sallow red mist chokes the realm.

sentences.zh: 咎在朕躬，今大將軍乃引過自予，欲上尚書事，歸大將軍印綬，罷大司馬官，是明朕之不德也。

translations.literal: The fault is on my person; now the great general draws the blame onto himself, wishes to return charge of the Masters of Writing, hand back the great general's seal-cord, and abolish the office of grand marshal—this would only advertise my lack of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is mine; yet the great general would shoulder the guilt himself, return the Masters of Writing, give back the seal and ribbon of general-in-chief, and strip the grand marshal's office—thus proclaiming my want of virtue.

sentences.zh: 朕委將軍以事，誠欲庶幾有成，顯先祖之功德。

translations.literal: I have entrusted you, general, with affairs because I earnestly hope for success and to display the merit and virtue of my ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: I charged you, General, with power because I hoped for achievement worthy of our forebears' deeds.

sentences.zh: 將軍其專心固意，輔朕之不逮，毋有所疑。」

translations.literal: General, fix your mind and steady your purpose; assist where I fall short, and harbor no doubts."
translations.idiomatic: Fix your resolve and steady your will; shore up my shortcomings and do not doubt my intent."

sentences.zh: 後五年，諸吏散騎安成侯崇薨，謚曰共侯。
有遺腹子奉世嗣侯，太后甚哀之。
明年，河平二年，上悉封舅譚為平阿侯，商成都侯，立紅陽侯，根曲陽侯，逢時高平侯。
五人同日封，故世謂之「五侯」。
太后同產唯曼蚤卒，余畢侯矣。
太后母李親，苟氏妻，生一男名參，寡居。
頃侯禁在時，太后令禁還李親。
太后憐參，欲以田□分為比而封之。
上曰：「封田氏，非正也。
」以參為侍中水衡都尉。
王氏子弟皆卿、大夫、侍中、諸曹，分據勢官滿朝廷。
大將軍鳳用事，上遂謙讓無所顓。

translations.literal: With the great general Feng wielding power, the emperor grew modest and claimed nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Feng held the reins, the emperor grew retiring and asserted nothing on his own.

sentences.zh: 左右常薦光祿大夫劉向少子歆通達有異材。

translations.literal: Those about him often recommended Liu Xin, youngest son of Grandee Liu Xiang, as learned and unusually talented.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants kept recommending Liu Xin, the younger son of Palace Grandee Liu Xiang, as learned and possessed of rare talent.

sentences.zh: 上召見歆，誦讀詩賦，甚說之，欲以為中常侍，召取衣冠。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Xin, listened to him recite poetry and rhapsodies, was greatly pleased, wished to make him palace attendant, and sent for cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Xin in, heard him intone poetry and fu, delighted in him, meant to appoint him palace attendant, and ordered his regalia brought.

sentences.zh: 臨當拜，左右皆曰：「未曉大將軍。

translations.literal: When the moment came to invest him, those about him all said: "We have not yet informed the great general.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of appointment they said, "The great general has not been consulted.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「此小事，何須關大將軍？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is a small matter—why must it concern the great general?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, "A trifle like this—why trouble the great general?

sentences.zh: 」左右叩頭爭之。

translations.literal: " Those about him kowtowed and argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed and argued him down.

sentences.zh: 上於是語鳳，鳳以為不可，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore spoke to Feng, who deemed it unacceptable, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke to Feng after all; Feng forbade it, and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 其見憚如此。

translations.literal: This is how much he was feared.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the fear he inspired.

sentences.zh: 上即位數年，無繼嗣，體常不平。

translations.literal: Several years into the reign the emperor had no heir and his health was often unsteady.
translations.idiomatic: A few years on the throne he still had no successor and his body was seldom robust.

sentences.zh: 定陶共王來朝，太后與上承先帝意，遇共王甚厚，賞賜十倍於它王，不以往事為纖介。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Dingtao came to court, the empress dowager and the emperor, following the late emperor's intent, treated the prince of Dingtao with great generosity, granting him ten times what other kings received, and they did not hold old grudges against him.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of joint Dingtao attended court, empress dowager and emperor, honoring the late emperor's wishes, lavished on him tenfold what other princes received and never nursed old slights.

sentences.zh: 共王之來朝也，天子留，不遣歸國。

translations.literal: When the prince of Dingtao came to court, the Son of Heaven kept him and would not let him return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: They detained him at the capital and would not send him home.

sentences.zh: 上謂共王：「我未有子，人命不諱，一朝有它，且不復相見。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the prince of Dingtao: "I have no son; men's lives admit no taboo—if something should happen one morning we might never meet again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "I have no son; fate does not promise long life—if I died tomorrow we might never meet again.

sentences.zh: 爾長留侍我矣！

translations.literal: You will stay long and wait on me!"
translations.idiomatic: Stay with me always!"

sentences.zh: 」其後，天子疾益有瘳，共王因留國邸，旦夕侍上，上甚親重。

translations.literal: After that the emperor's illness improved somewhat, and the prince of Dingtao therefore stayed in the state guesthouse, attending morning and evening; the emperor grew very close to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then rallied; the prince lodged in the capital guesthouse, attending him day and night, and grew dearer than ever.

sentences.zh: 大將軍鳳心不便共王在京師，會日蝕，鳳因言：「日蝕，陰盛之象，為非常異。

translations.literal: The great general Feng was ill at ease with the prince of Dingtao remaining in the capital; when a solar eclipse occurred, Feng therefore said: "A solar eclipse is the image of yin prevailing—an extraordinary anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng disliked keeping the prince at the capital; when an eclipse came he declared, "An eclipse shows yin ascendant—an omen outside the norm.

sentences.zh: 定陶王雖親，於禮當奉籓在國。

translations.literal: The prince of Dingtao is kin, but by ritual he ought to hold his fief in his state.
translations.idiomatic: Joint Dingtao is family, yet rite says a prince should keep to his domain.

sentences.zh: 今留侍京師，詭正非常，故天見戒。

translations.literal: Now he stays to wait on the capital—against proper rule and outside the norm—therefore heaven has shown its warning.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping him here bends the rule and invites heaven's rebuke.

sentences.zh: 宜遣王之國。

translations.literal: He ought to be sent to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Send him back to his fief.

sentences.zh: 」上不得已於鳳而許之。

translations.literal: " The emperor, unable to refuse Feng, consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, unable to gainsay Feng, agreed.

sentences.zh: 共王辭去，上與相對涕泣而決。

translations.literal: The prince of Dingtao took his leave; the emperor faced him weeping and parted in tears.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince departed, emperor and kinsman wept face to face at their parting.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹王章素剛直敢言，以為鳳建遣共王之國非是，乃奏封事言日蝕之咎矣。

translations.literal: Wang Zhang, governor of the capital, was by nature blunt and outspoken; he thought Feng wrong to have urged sending the prince of Dingtao to his state and therefore submitted a sealed memorial saying the blame for the eclipse lay elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang, governor of the capital, was blunt by nature; he believed Feng wrong to banish the prince of Dingtao and filed a sealed note arguing the eclipse augured something else.

sentences.zh: 天子召見章，延問以事，章對曰：「天道聰明，佑善而災惡，以瑞異為符效。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven summoned Zhang and prolonged the interview on the matter; Zhang replied: "Heaven's way is clear-sighted; it aids the good and punishes evil, using auspicious and strange signs as tokens.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called him in and pressed him; Wang Zhang said, "Heaven is clear-sighted: it blesses the good and smites the wicked, marking them with omens.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以未有繼嗣，引近定陶王，所以承宗廟，重社稷，上順天心，下安百姓。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, having no heir, has drawn the prince of Dingtao near to continue the ancestral shrines and weight the altars of soil and grain—this accords with high heaven above and steadies the people below.
translations.idiomatic: You lack an heir, so you have drawn the prince of Dingtao close to sustain the temples and secure the altars—above this answers heaven, below it steadies the people.

sentences.zh: 此正義善事，當有祥瑞，何故致災異？

translations.literal: This is righteous and good; there ought to be auspicious signs—why then bring down disasters and anomalies?
translations.idiomatic: That is just and good; one should expect felicity—why should it breed portents of ill?

sentences.zh: 災異之發，為大臣顓政者也。

translations.literal: When disasters and anomalies arise, it is because great ministers monopolize government.
translations.idiomatic: When ill omens come, it is because powerful ministers hold all authority.

sentences.zh: 今聞大將軍猥歸日蝕之咎於定陶王，建遣之國，苟欲使天子孤立於上，顓擅朝事以便其私，非忠臣也。

translations.literal: Now I hear the great general basely shifts blame for the eclipse onto the prince of Dingtao and urges him sent to his state, merely wishing to leave the Son of Heaven isolated aloft and monopolize court business to suit his private ends—not the conduct of a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the great general meanly pins the eclipse on the prince and drives him home, wanting the emperor isolated aloft so he can run the court for private gain—that is not loyal service.

sentences.zh: 且日蝕，陰侵陽、臣顓君之咎，今政事大小皆自鳳出，天子曾不一舉手，鳳不內省責，反歸咎善人，推遠定陶王。

translations.literal: Moreover a solar eclipse means yin encroaching on yang and ministers dominating their lord; now great and small policy all issues from Feng alone, and the Son of Heaven has not once raised a hand; Feng does not look inward to blame himself but turns on good men and pushes the prince of Dingtao away.
translations.idiomatic: An eclipse means yin eating at yang and subjects lording over the ruler; today every decision flows from Feng while the emperor lifts not a finger; Feng does not search his own heart but blames the innocent and drives the prince off.

sentences.zh: 且鳳誣罔不忠，非一事也。

translations.literal: Moreover Feng has been false and disloyal in more than one matter.
translations.idiomatic: Nor is this Feng's only deceit or disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 前丞相樂昌侯商本以先帝外屬，內行篤，有威重，位歷將相，國家柱石臣也，其人守正，不肯詘節隨鳳委曲，卒用閨門之事為鳳所罷，身以憂死，眾庶愍之。

translations.literal: The former chancellor, Marquis of Lechang Shang, was by origin an in-law of the former emperor; inwardly he was steadfast and carried weight; he had risen through general to minister and was a pillar of the state; the man held to the straight path and would not bend to follow Feng's twists, and in the end Feng removed him on a matter of the women's quarters; he died of grief and the common people pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: The late chancellor, Marquis of Lechang Wang Shang, came from the previous emperor's maternal kin; inwardly he was solid and commanded respect, having served as general and minister—a pillar of the state. He kept the straight course and would not truckle to Feng's intrigues, so Feng ousted him over a boudoir scandal; he died of sorrow and the people mourned him.

sentences.zh: 又鳳知其小婦弟張美人已嘗適人，於禮不宜配御至尊，托以為宜子，內之後宮，苟以私其妻弟。

translations.literal: Moreover Feng knew that his younger concubine's younger sister, Lady Zhang, had already been married to another man and by ritual ought not attend the supreme one; he falsely claimed she would bear sons and placed her in the rear palace, merely to favor his wife's brother.
translations.idiomatic: Feng also knew his junior concubine's sister, the Zhang lady, had already been another man's wife and by rite must not serve the sovereign; yet he pretended she would bear sons and slipped her into the harem to please his brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 聞張美人未嘗任身就館也。

translations.literal: I have heard that Lady Zhang has never conceived or gone to the lying-in lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Word is she has never quickened with child or entered the birth hall.

sentences.zh: 且羌胡尚殺首子以蕩腸正世，況於天子而近已出之女也！

translations.literal: Moreover the Qiang and Hu still kill the firstborn to purge the womb and set the world right—how much the less may the Son of Heaven take near him a woman who has already borne a child elsewhere!
translations.idiomatic: Even Qiang and Hu slay firstborns to cleanse the line—how much more must the Son of Heaven shun a woman already another man's issue!

sentences.zh: 此三者皆大事，陛下所自見，足以知其餘，及它所不見者。

translations.literal: These three are great matters that Your Majesty has seen with your own eyes; they are enough to know the rest and what you have not seen.
translations.idiomatic: These three are weighty affairs you have witnessed yourself; from them you may infer the rest, and what lies beyond your sight.

sentences.zh: 鳳不可令久典事，宜退使就第，選忠賢以代之。」

translations.literal: Feng must not be left long in charge; he should retire to his mansion and loyal worthies be chosen to replace him."
translations.idiomatic: Feng cannot hold power indefinitely; send him home to his estate and put honest men in his place."

sentences.zh: 自鳳之白罷商後遣定陶王也，上不能平。

translations.literal: From the time Feng had forced Shang out and then sent the prince of Dingtao away, the emperor had not been reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Feng cashiered Shang and packed the prince of Dingtao off, the emperor had nursed a grievance.

sentences.zh: 及聞章言，天子感寤，納之，謂章曰：「微京兆尹直言，吾不聞社稷計！

translations.literal: When he heard Zhang's words, the emperor was moved to understanding, accepted them, and said to Zhang: "Were it not for the governor of the capital speaking straight, I would not have heard counsel for the altars!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Wang Zhang, he woke to the truth and said, "Without your blunt speech I would never have heard advice for the realm!

sentences.zh: 且唯賢知賢，君試為朕求可以自輔者。

translations.literal: Moreover only the worthy know the worthy; you try to find for Us someone who may aid Us.
translations.idiomatic: Only the worthy recognize worth—find me someone fit to strengthen my hand.

sentences.zh: 」於是章奏封事，薦中山孝王舅琅邪太守馮野王「先帝時歷二卿，忠信質直，知謀有餘。

translations.literal: " Zhang therefore submitted a sealed memorial recommending Feng Yewang, maternal uncle of Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, governor of Langye—"in the former emperor's time he had twice served as a minister; he is loyal, trustworthy, plain, and straight, with more than enough counsel and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang then sealed a memorial recommending Feng Yewang, uncle of the prince of Zhongshan and governor of Langye: "Under the late emperor he twice held ministerial rank; he is loyal, plain, and straight, with counsel to spare.

sentences.zh: 野王以王舅出，以賢復人，明聖主樂進賢也。

translations.literal: Yewang had left office because he was the king's maternal uncle; to recall him for his worth shows how a sage ruler delights in promoting the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yewang had been cashiered as the prince's uncle; bringing him back on merit proved a clear-sighted sovereign's love of advancing good men.

sentences.zh: 」上自為太子時數聞野王先帝名卿，聲譽出鳳遠甚，方倚欲以代鳳。

translations.literal: "Since I was heir apparent I have often heard Yewang named among the former emperor's eminent ministers; his repute outstripped Feng's by far, and I was leaning on him to replace Feng."
translations.idiomatic: Even as crown prince he had heard Yewang praised among the late emperor's great ministers—his name shone far above Feng's—and he had meant to lean on Yewang as Feng's successor.

sentences.zh: 初，章每召見，上輒辟左右。

translations.literal: At first, whenever Zhang was summoned, the emperor always dismissed those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Wang Zhang came to audience, the emperor cleared the room of attendants.

sentences.zh: 時太后從弟長樂衛尉弘子侍中音獨側聽，具知章言，以語鳳。

translations.literal: At that time Yin, palace attendant and son of Hong, commandant of the guards at Changle-the empress dowager's patrilateral cousin-alone listened from the side, learned all Zhang's words in full, and reported them to Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin, palace attendant and son of Wang Hong, the Changle guard commandant who was the empress dowager's cousin, eavesdropped alone, heard every word, and carried it all to Wang Feng.

sentences.zh: 鳳聞之，稱病出就第，上疏乞骸骨，謝上曰：「臣材駑愚戇，得以外屬兄弟七人封為列侯，宗族蒙恩，賞賜無量。

translations.literal: When Feng heard this, he claimed illness, withdrew to his mansion, and submitted a memorial begging leave to retire, apologizing to the emperor: "Your servant's talents are dull, foolish, and blunt; yet seven brothers of the outer kin were enfeoffed as full marquises; the clan has received grace beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Feng feigned sickness, retired home, and sent up a groveling memorial: "I am a dull, blunt man, yet seven brothers of the affinal house became full marquises; the whole clan has drunk deep of imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 輔政出入七年，國家委任臣鳳，所言輒聽，薦士常用。

translations.literal: For seven years in and out of government the state has entrusted your servant Feng; whatever he said was obeyed, and the men he recommended were constantly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years I have helped govern; the court has hung on my word, and every man I pushed forward won a post.

sentences.zh: 無一功善，陰陽不調，災異數見，咎在臣鳳奉職無狀，此臣一當退也。

translations.literal: There has been no single good achievement; yin and yang are not in harmony and disasters and anomalies have repeatedly appeared; the fault lies with your servant Feng's unsatisfactory discharge of duty-this is the first reason I ought to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: I have done nothing truly good; yin and yang stay out of tune and omens pile up—the fault is mine in office. That is my first reason to step down.

sentences.zh: 《五經》傳記，師所誦說，咸以日蝕之咎在於大臣非其人，《易》曰『折其右肱』，此臣二當退也。

translations.literal: In the transmitted texts and records of the Five Classics, what masters recite and expound all hold that blame for a solar eclipse lies with great ministers who are not the right men; the Changes says 'Break his right arm'-this is the second reason I ought to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Classics and their commentaries all say an eclipse indicts ministers unfit for their posts; the Book of Changes speaks of breaking the right arm—that is my second reason to retire.

sentences.zh: 河平以來，臣久病連年，數出在外，曠職素餐，此臣三當退也。

translations.literal: Since Heping I have been ill for years on end, repeatedly absent abroad from duty, neglecting office while drawing pay-this is the third reason I ought to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Since Heping I have lingered sick, often away from my desk, eating salary without earning it—my third cause to go.

sentences.zh: 陛下以皇太后故不忍誅廢，臣猶自知當遠流放，又重自念，兄弟宗族所蒙不測，當殺身靡骨死輦轂下，不當以無益之故有離寢門之心，誠歲余以來，所苦加侵，日日益甚，不勝大願，願乞骸骨，歸自治養，冀賴陛下神靈，未埋發齒，期月之間，幸得瘳愈，復望帷幄，不然，必置溝壑。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, for the empress dowager's sake, cannot bear to execute or dismiss me; your servant still knows he ought to be banished to a distant place; yet again I think how immeasurably my brothers and clan have been favored-I ought to grind my bones to dust and die beneath the imperial carriage-yet I ought not, for a useless reason, harbor a heart that leaves the bedchamber gate; truly, over the past year the illness that has tormented me has pressed harder day by day; I cannot bear my great longing; I beg to surrender my bones and return home to nurse myself, trusting in Your Majesty's numinous power-before my hair and teeth are yet buried, within a month or so I may perhaps recover and again hope to attend within the curtains; if not, I must be cast into ditch and gully.
translations.idiomatic: You spare me execution for the empress dowager's sake, yet I know I deserve exile. Still I remember how boundlessly my kinsmen have been enriched—I should grind myself to dust under your wheels—yet I must not, on a petty pretext, turn my back on the inner palace. For more than a year my sickness has worsened daily; I can bear it no longer. Grant me my bones to heal at home; if your spirit wills it, before I am in the grave I may in a month or two rally and again serve within the curtain; if not, cast me out to rot.

sentences.zh: 臣以非材見私，天下知臣受恩深也；

translations.literal: Your servant, though unworthy, has been shown private favor; the realm knows how deeply your servant has received grace.
translations.idiomatic: The world knows how deeply you have favored a man of no real talent.

sentences.zh: 以病得全骸骨歸，天下知臣被恩見哀，重巍巍也。

translations.literal: To obtain my whole bones back home on account of illness lets the realm know your servant has been shown pity in his grace-how weighty that is.
translations.idiomatic: Letting me go home whole on grounds of sickness will show the empire the depth of your mercy.

sentences.zh: 進退於國為厚，萬無纖介之議。

translations.literal: Whether I advance or retire, it will be a gain to the state; there will be not the slightest grumbling.
translations.idiomatic: Either way the state is richer for it, and no one will whisper complaint.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下哀憐！

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty pity me!"
translations.idiomatic: Only pity me, Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 」其辭指甚哀，太后聞之為垂涕，不御食。

translations.literal: The wording was exceedingly piteous; when the empress dowager heard it she wept and would not take her meal.
translations.idiomatic: The plea was heart-rending; the empress dowager wept at the news and refused her meal.

sentences.zh: 上少而親倚鳳，弗忍廢，乃報鳳曰：「朕秉事不明，政事多闕，故天變婁臻，咸在朕躬。

translations.literal: The emperor had relied on Feng from youth and could not bear to dismiss him; he therefore replied to Feng: "We have been unclear in handling affairs; government has many gaps; therefore heaven's changes have come thick and fast-all lie on Our person.
translations.idiomatic: Raised under Feng's wing, the emperor could not cast him off and answered: "My rule has been dim and the administration full of holes; heaven's warnings come one after another—the fault is mine alone.

sentences.zh: 將軍乃深引過自予，欲乞骸骨而退，則朕將何向焉！

translations.literal: For the great general deeply to draw blame onto himself and wish to beg his bones and retire-then whither shall We turn!
translations.idiomatic: If you shoulder every fault and beg to retire, where am I to turn?

sentences.zh: 《書》不雲乎？

translations.literal: Does not the Documents say?
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Book of Documents say?

sentences.zh: 『公毋困我』。

translations.literal: 'Do not, my duke, beset me.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Do not, my duke, beset me.'

sentences.zh: 務專精神，安心自持，期於亟廖，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: Concentrate your spirit, calm your mind and hold yourself steady; look to swift recovery; this matches Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Gather your strength, quiet your heart, and mend in haste—that is what I wish of you."

sentences.zh: 」於是鳳起視事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Feng rose and resumed handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Feng left his sickbed and returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 上使尚書劾奏章：「知野王前以王舅出補吏，而私薦之，欲令在朝阿附諸侯；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Masters of Writing to impeach Zhang: "He knew Yewang had earlier been sent out as a clerk because he was the king's maternal uncle, yet privately recommended him, wishing to have him at court to curry favor with the princes;
translations.idiomatic: He had the Masters of Writing indict Wang Zhang: "Zhang knew Yewang had been demoted to a local post as the prince's uncle, yet privately pushed his recall, scheming to plant him at court to toady to the feudatories.

sentences.zh: 又知張美人體御至尊，而妄稱引羌胡殺子蕩腸，非所宜言。

translations.literal: he also knew the Lady Zhang had lain with the supreme one, yet recklessly cited the Qiang and Hu killing the firstborn to purge the womb-not words fit to speak.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the Zhang lady had shared the sovereign's couch, yet wildly invoked barbarians slaying firstborns—speech unfit for a subject.

sentences.zh: 」遂下章吏。

translations.literal: " He thereupon handed Zhang over to the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was handed to the judicial clerks.

sentences.zh: 廷尉致其大逆罪，以為「比上夷狄，欲絕繼嗣之端；

translations.literal: The commandant of justice charged him with the great crime of rebellion, holding that "he ranked himself with the barbarians of the north, wishing to cut off the thread of heirs;
translations.idiomatic: The commandant of justice framed a charge of great treason: "He likened the throne to barbarian ways and meant to sever the line of succession.

sentences.zh: 背畔天子，私為定陶王。

translations.literal: he turned his back on the Son of Heaven and secretly acted for the prince of Dingtao."
translations.idiomatic: He turned his back on the Son of Heaven and secretly worked the prince of Dingtao's interest."

sentences.zh: 」章死獄中，妻子徙合浦。

translations.literal: Zhang died in prison; his wife and children were banished to Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang died in jail; his family was transported to Hepu.

sentences.zh: 自是公卿見鳳，側目而視，郡國守相、刺吏皆出其門。

translations.literal: From this time the dukes and ministers, when they saw Feng, looked askance; governors and shepherds of commanderies and kingdoms and regional inspectors all issued from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: After that every minister met Feng with sidelong glances; commandery and kingdom governors and regional inspectors all owed their posts to his door.

sentences.zh: 又以侍中太僕音為御史大夫，列於三公。

translations.literal: He also appointed Yin, palace attendant and grand coachman, as imperial counselor, ranking among the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, palace attendant and grand coachman, was made imperial counselor—one of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 而五侯群弟，爭為奢移，賂遺珍寶，四面而至；

translations.literal: Moreover the five marquises' band of younger brothers vied in extravagance and excess; bribes and gifts of precious treasures arrived from every quarter;
translations.idiomatic: The five brothers outdid one another in waste and display; treasures poured in from every direction as bribes.

sentences.zh: 後廷姬妾，各數十人，僮奴以千百數，羅鐘馨，舞鄭女，作倡優，狗馬馳逐；

translations.literal: the rear palace's concubines numbered several tens each, boy and girl slaves by the hundreds and thousands; they strung bells and chimes, danced Zheng girls, put on actors and jesters, and raced dogs and horses;
translations.idiomatic: Their rear halls swarmed with dozens of concubines each and hundreds or thousands of slaves; bells and stone chimes rang, dancers from Zheng performed, actors capered, dogs and horses raced the grounds.

sentences.zh: 大治第室，起土山漸臺，洞門高廊閣道，連屬彌望。

translations.literal: they greatly built mansions, raised earthen hills and terraced towers, tunnel gates and high corridors and connecting galleries, stretching as far as the eye could see.
translations.idiomatic: They threw up vast compounds—earthen mounds, terraced belvederes, arched gateways, lofty cloisters, and linked galleries that ran to the horizon.

sentences.zh: 百姓歌之曰：「五侯初起，曲陽最怒，壞決高都，連竟外杜，土山漸臺西白虎。

translations.literal: The common people sang of them: "When the five marquises first rose, Quyang was fiercest of all; he broke through Gaodu, linked clear to Waidu beyond; west of the earthen hill and terraced tower, the White Tiger."
translations.idiomatic: The people sang: "When the five marquises first rose, Quyang was worst—he burst the Gaodu dyke, linked channel to outer Waidu; west of the mound and tower stood the White Tiger hall."

sentences.zh: 」其奢僭如此。

translations.literal: Their extravagance and presumption were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Their presumption and waste reached that pitch.

sentences.zh: 然皆通敏人事，好士養賢，傾財施予，以相高尚。

translations.literal: Yet they were all quick and perceptive in human affairs, fond of scholars and nurturing worthies, pouring out wealth in largesse to vie in nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were shrewd with men, patronized scholars, poured gold on guests, and vied to seem high-minded.

sentences.zh: 鳳輔政凡十一歲。

translations.literal: Feng assisted government in all for eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng held the reins eleven years.

sentences.zh: 陽朔三年秋，鳳疾，天子數自臨問，親執其手，涕泣曰：「將軍病，如有不可言，平阿侯譚次將軍矣。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Yangshuo, Feng fell ill; the Son of Heaven repeatedly came in person to inquire, grasped his hand, and weeping said: "If the general's illness should have an unspeakable outcome, Marquis of Ping'e Tan is next after the general."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn of Yangshuo 3, as Feng sickened, the emperor visited again and again, took his hand in tears, and said, "If the worst should come, Marquis of Ping'e Tan succeeds you as chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」鳳頓首泣曰：「譚等雖與臣至親，行皆奢僭，無以率導百姓，不如御史大夫音謹敕，臣敢以死保之。

translations.literal: Feng kowtowed weeping and said: "Though Tan and the others are as close to your servant as flesh, their conduct is all extravagant and presumptuous; they have no way to lead the hundred clans-not like Imperial Counselor Yin, who is scrupulous and restrained; your servant dares guarantee him with his life."
translations.idiomatic: Feng kowtowed in tears: "Tan and his brothers are kin, yet every one of them is reckless and overweening—useless as models for the people. Yin the imperial counselor is careful and sober; I stake my life on him."

sentences.zh: 」及鳳且死，上疏謝上，復固薦音自代，言譚等五人必不可用。

translations.literal: When Feng was near death he submitted a memorial thanking the emperor and again firmly recommended Yin to replace himself, saying Tan and the other five could in no case be employed.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he thanked the throne and pressed Yin again as his sole successor, insisting the five brothers must never be given power.

sentences.zh: 天子然之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，譚倨，不肯事鳳，而音敬鳳，卑恭如子，故薦之。
鳳薨，天子臨吊贈寵，送以輕車介士，軍陳自長安至渭陵，謚曰敬成侯。
子襄嗣侯，為衛尉。
御史大夫音竟代鳳為大司馬車騎將軍，而平阿侯譚位特進，領城門兵。
谷永說譚，令讓不受城門職，由是與音不平，語在《永傳》。
音既以從舅越親用事，小心親職，歲餘，上下詔曰：「車騎將軍音宿衛忠正，勤勞國家，前為御史大夫，以外親宜典兵馬，入為將軍，不獲宰相之封，朕甚慊焉！

translations.literal: Yin, because he was a maternal uncle once removed and ever closer, wielded power with care and close attention to duty; after more than a year the emperor issued an edict: "General of chariots and cavalry Yin has long guarded the palace with loyalty and rectitude and toiled for the state; formerly he was imperial counselor; as affinal kin he was fit to command horse and foot, and entered as general without receiving a chancellor's fief-We are much displeased at that!
translations.idiomatic: Once Yin took power—as a closer cousin on the distaff side—he served with caution. A year later the edict ran: "The general of chariots and cavalry has long kept loyal night watch and worn himself out for the realm; he was once imperial counselor; as in-law he was rightly given troops, then raised to general, yet never got a chancellor's reward—I regret that deeply.

sentences.zh: 其封音為安陽侯，食邑與五侯等，俱三千戶。」

translations.literal: Enfeoff Yin as marquis of Anyang with revenue equal to the five marquises, each three thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: Make Yin marquis of Anyang with three thousand households, matching the five brothers' fiefs."

sentences.zh: 初，成都侯商嘗病，欲避暑，從上借明光宮，後又穿長安城，引內澧水注第中大陂以行船，立羽蓋，張周帷，輯濯越歌。

translations.literal: At first, Marquis of Chengdu Shang once fell ill and wished to escape the heat; he borrowed Bright Light Palace from the emperor, then later tunneled through the walls of Chang'an, led the Li River within to fill a great pond in his mansion so he could sail boats, set up feathered canopies, stretched Zhou-style curtains, and had the oarsmen sing the Yue song.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Chengdu Wang Shang once sought relief from summer heat: he borrowed Bright Light Palace from the throne, then cut through the capital wall, diverted the Li into his estate to float pleasure boats, raised feathered canopies, hung silken curtains, and set oarsmen chanting Yue boat songs.

sentences.zh: 上幸商第，見穿城引水，意恨，內銜之，未言。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Shang's mansion and saw the tunnel through the city and the diversion of water, he felt resentment and inwardly harbored anger but said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial visit showed the breach in the wall and the canal—rage coiled in the emperor's breast, though he held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 後微行出，過曲陽侯第，又見園中土山漸臺似類白虎殿。

translations.literal: Later, on a private outing, he passed the mansion of Marquis of Quyang and again saw in the garden an earthen hill and terraced tower resembling the White Tiger Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later, traveling incognito, he passed Quyang's villa and saw a mound and terrace that mimicked the palace White Tiger Hall.

sentences.zh: 於是上怒，以讓車騎將軍音。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor grew angry and rebuked General of chariots and cavalry Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He burst out and rebuked General Yin.

sentences.zh: 商、根兄弟欲自黥、劓謝太后。

translations.literal: Shang and Gen, brothers, wished to tattoo and cut off their own noses to apologize to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Shang and Gen offered to mutilate themselves—tattoo and clipped nose—to appease the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 上聞之大怒，乃使尚書責問司隸校尉、京兆尹：「知成都侯商擅穿帝城，決引澧水，曲陽侯根驕奢僭上，赤墀青瑣，紅陽侯立父子臧匿奸猾亡命，賓客為群盜，司隸、京兆皆阿縱不舉奏正法。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he was greatly angered and ordered the Masters of Reading to upbraid the colonel of the region and the governor of the capital: "You knew Marquis of Chengdu Shang presumptuously tunneled through the imperial city and cut the Li to lead it in; Marquis of Quyang Gen was arrogant and presumptuous toward the sovereign, with cinnabar steps and green jade door-bolts; Marquis of Hongyang Li and his son harbored crafty fugitives from the law, and their guests formed bandit gangs-yet the colonel and the governor of the capital both connived and did not memorialize to apply the law."
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Masters of Reading to flay the metropolitan colonel and the governor of the capital: "You knew Chengdu had breached the imperial wall and tapped the Li; Quyang flaunted cinnabar steps and green latches above his rank; Hongyang hid wanted criminals whose retainers turned bandit—yet you winked at it all and filed no charge."

sentences.zh: 」二人頓首省戶下。

translations.literal: The two men kowtowed beneath the door of the privy chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Both men kowtowed at the chamber door.

sentences.zh: 又賜車騎將軍音策書曰：「外家何甘樂禍敗，而欲自黥、劓，相戮辱於太后前，傷慈母之心，以危亂國！

translations.literal: He also bestowed on General of chariots and cavalry Yin a rescript: "Why should the outer kin gladly court ruin and wish to tattoo and cut their noses, mutilating and shaming one another before the empress dowager, wounding a loving mother's heart and endangering the state!
translations.idiomatic: His rescript to General Yin ran: "Why does the affinal house court disaster, begging to scar and slash one another before the dowager, breaking a mother's heart and shaking the realm?

sentences.zh: 外家宗族強，上一身寢弱日久，今將一施之。

translations.literal: The outer kin's clan is strong; the sovereign's single body has lain weak a long time-now We shall apply the rod once for all.
translations.idiomatic: The in-laws have grown too mighty while I have long been frail—now I will strike once, hard.

sentences.zh: 君其召諸侯，令待府捨。

translations.literal: You shall summon the marquises and order them to wait at the ministry lodging."
translations.idiomatic: Summon every marquis and hold them at the ministry compound."

sentences.zh: 」是日，詔尚書奏文帝時誅將軍薄昭故事。

translations.literal: That day he ordered the Masters of Reading to memorialize the precedent from Wendi's time of executing General Bo Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he told the Masters of Reading to cite Emperor Wen's execution of General Bo Zhao.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍音藉槁請罪，商、立、根皆負斧質謝。

translations.literal: General of chariots and cavalry Yin spread straw and begged pardon; Shang, Li, and Gen all bore axe and executioner's block to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Yin threw himself on straw matting to beg mercy; Shang, Li, and Gen came with axe and stake on their backs.

sentences.zh: 上不忍誅，然後得已。

translations.literal: The emperor could not bear to execute them, and only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 久之，平阿侯譚薨，謚曰安侯，子仁嗣侯。

translations.literal: After a long while Marquis of Ping'e Tan died; he was posthumously titled Marquis An; his son Ren succeeded the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Marquis of Ping'e Tan died, posthumously honored as Marquis An; his son Ren inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 太后憐弟曼蚤死，獨不封，曼寡婦渠供養東宮，子莽幼孤不及等比，常以為語。

translations.literal: The empress dowager pitied her younger brother Man, who had died early and alone had received no fief; Man's widow Qu supported the Eastern Palace, and her son Mang was a young orphan who had not been ranked with the others-she often spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager grieved for her brother Man, dead young and never ennobled; his widow Qu served the Eastern Palace, and young Mang had been passed over—she never ceased mentioning it.

sentences.zh: 平阿侯譚、成都侯商及在位多稱莽者。

translations.literal: Marquis of Ping'e Tan, Marquis of Chengdu Shang, and many who held office praised Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan of Ping'e, Shang of Chengdu, and other men in power all spoke well of Mang.

sentences.zh: 久之，上復下詔追封曼為新都哀侯，而子莽嗣爵為新都侯。

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor again issued an edict posthumously enfeoffing Man as Marquis Ai of Xindu, while his son Mang succeeded the title as marquis of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: At length an edict posthumously made Man Marquis Ai of Xindu, and Mang inherited as marquis of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 後又封太后姊子淳天長為定陵侯。

translations.literal: Later he also enfeoffed Chunyu Chang, son of the empress dowager's elder sister, as marquis of Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: He later enfeoffed Chunyu Chang—son of the dowager's elder sister—as marquis of Dingling.

sentences.zh: 王氏親屬，侯者凡十人。

translations.literal: In all ten persons of Wang affinal kin held marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Ten Wang in-laws now held marquises.

sentences.zh: 上悔廢平阿侯譚不輔政而薨也，乃復進成都侯商以特進，領城門兵，置幕府，得舉吏如將軍。
杜鄴說車騎將軍音令親附商，語在《鄴傳》。
王氏爵位日盛，唯音為修整，數諫正，有忠節，輔政八年，薨。
吊贈如大將軍，謚曰敬侯。
子舜嗣侯，為太僕侍中。
特進成都侯商代音為大司馬衛將軍，而紅陽侯立位特進，領城門兵。
商輔政四歲，病乞骸骨，天子憫之，更以為大將軍，益封二千戶，賜錢百萬。
商薨，吊贈如大將軍故事，謚曰景成侯，子況嗣侯。
紅陽侯立次當輔政，有罪過，語在《孫寶傳》。
上乃廢立，而用光祿勳曲陽侯根為大司馬票騎將軍，歲余益封千七百戶。
高平侯逢時無材能名稱，是歲薨，謚曰戴侯，子買之嗣侯。
綏和元年，上即位二十餘年無繼嗣，而定陶共王已薨，子嗣立為王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Suihe the emperor had been on the throne more than twenty years without an heir, and the prince of joint Dingtao had died; his son succeeded as king.
translations.idiomatic: Suihe 1: twenty-odd years on the throne still without an heir; the prince of joint Dingtao was dead and his son now ruled the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 王祖母定陶傅太后重賂遺票騎將軍根，為王求漢嗣，根為言，上亦欲立之，遂徵定陶王為太子。

translations.literal: The king's grandmother, Grand Empress Dowager Fu of Dingtao, heavily bribed General of agile cavalry Gen to seek the Han succession for the king; Gen spoke for him, and the emperor also wished to establish him-thereupon he summoned the prince of Dingtao as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's grandmother, Lady Fu of Dingtao, stuffed General Gen's pockets to win the crown for her grandson; Gen spoke in his favor, the emperor concurred, and the prince of Dingtao was summoned as heir.

sentences.zh: 時根輔政五歲矣，乞骸骨，上乃益封根五千戶，賜安車駟馬，黃金五百斤，罷就第。

translations.literal: At that time Gen had assisted government five years; he begged his bones, and the emperor therefore added five thousand households to Gen's fief, bestowed a comfortable carriage and four horses, five hundred jin of gold, and dismissed him to his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Gen had governed five years; he asked to retire. The emperor added five thousand households to his fief, gave him a state carriage, four horses, five hundred jin of gold, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 先是，定陵侯淳于長以外屬能謀議，為衛尉侍中，在輔政之次。

translations.literal: Earlier, Marquis of Dingling Chunyu Chang, as affinal kin able to counsel, had been commandant of the guards and palace attendant, second in assisting government.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chunyu Chang of Dingling, an in-law skilled in intrigue, had been commandant of the guards and palace attendant—second only to the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 是歲，新都侯莽告長伏罪與紅陽侯立相連，長下獄死，立就國，語在《長傳》。

translations.literal: That year Marquis of Xindu Mang reported Chang's hidden crimes as linked with Marquis of Hongyang Li; Chang was cast into prison and died, Li went to his state-the account is in Chang's biography.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mang denounced Chang's secret crimes tied to Li of Hongyang; Chang died in prison, Li was sent to his fief—the tale is told in Chang's biography.

sentences.zh: 故曲陽侯根薦莽以自代，上亦以為莽有忠直節，遂擢莽從侍中騎都尉光祿大夫為大司馬。

translations.literal: Therefore Marquis of Quyang Gen recommended Mang to replace himself; the emperor also thought Mang possessed loyalty and upright integrity-thereupon he promoted Mang from palace attendant and chief of cavalry and grandee of brilliant virtue to grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Quyang's Gen then backed Mang as his successor; the emperor too saw loyalty in Mang and raised him from palace attendant, chief of cavalry, and grandee of brilliant virtue to grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，成帝崩，哀帝即位。

translations.literal: After more than a year Emperor Cheng died and Emperor Ai ascended.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Cheng died and Ai took the throne.

sentences.zh: 太后詔莽就第，避帝外家。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered Mang to go to his mansion and yield place to the emperor's maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager told Mang to retire home and clear the field for the new emperor's maternal relatives.

sentences.zh: 哀帝初優莽，不聽。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Ai treated Mang generously and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ai favored Mang and refused.

sentences.zh: 莽上書固乞骸骨而退。

translations.literal: Mang submitted a memorial firmly begging his bones to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Mang pressed a memorial, begging to retire in earnest.

sentences.zh: 上乃下詔曰：「曲陽侯根前在位，建社稷策。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon issued an edict: "Marquis of Quyang Gen formerly held office and framed policies for the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered: "Quyang's Gen once set state policy from high office.

sentences.zh: 侍中太僕安陽侯舜往時護太子家，導朕，忠誠專一，有舊恩。

translations.literal: Palace attendant and grand coachman Marquis of Anyang Shun in the past guarded the heir's household and guided Us, loyal and single-minded, with old kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Anyang's Shun, palace attendant and grand coachman, once guarded the heir's house and guided me with steadfast old devotion.

sentences.zh: 新都侯莽憂勞國家，執義堅固，庶幾與為治，太皇太后詔休就第，朕甚閔焉。

translations.literal: Marquis of Xindu Mang has worried and toiled for the state, holding to righteous firmness; We had hoped to govern with him; the grand empress dowager's edict ordered him to rest at his mansion-We greatly pity that.
translations.idiomatic: Xindu's Mang has worn himself out for the realm, clinging to principle; I meant to rule with him until the grand empress dowager ordered him home—I grieve for that.

sentences.zh: 其益封根二千戶，舜五百戶，莽三百五十戶。

translations.literal: Add two thousand households to Gen, five hundred to Shun, three hundred fifty to Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Add two thousand households to Gen, five hundred to Shun, three hundred fifty to Mang.

sentences.zh: 以莽為特進，朝朔望。

translations.literal: Make Mang specially advanced, to attend court on the first and fifteenth.
translations.idiomatic: Advance Mang to specially advanced rank with audience on new and full moons."

sentences.zh: 」又還紅陽侯立京師。

translations.literal: He also returned Marquis of Hongyang Li to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Li of Hongyang to the capital.

sentences.zh: 哀帝少而聞知五氏驕盛，心不能善，以初立，故優之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai had heard from youth of the five Wangs' arrogance and could not approve; because he had newly ascended he therefore treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Young Ai had grown up hearing how the five Wang swaggered; he disliked them, yet as a new sovereign he still indulged them.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，司隸校尉解光奏：「曲陽侯根宗重身尊，三世據權，五將秉政，天下輻湊自效。

translations.literal: After more than a month Colonel of the region Xie Guang memorialized: "Marquis of Quyang Gen's clan is weighty and his person honored; for three generations they have held power, five generals have wielded government, and the realm has crowded in to offer service.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Colonel Xie Guang charged: "Gen of Quyang's clan is mighty and his person exalted; three generations have gripped power, five generals have run the court, and the empire has flocked to do his bidding.

sentences.zh: 根行貪邪，臧累巨萬，縱橫恣意，大治室第，第中起土山，立兩市，殿上赤墀，戶青瑣；

translations.literal: Gen's conduct has been greedy and depraved; his ill-gotten wealth runs to tens of millions; he has ranged at will, greatly built chambers and halls, raised an earthen hill inside the compound, set up two market wards, cinnabar steps on the hall, and green jade bolts on the doors;
translations.idiomatic: He is greedy and corrupt, his hidden treasure reckoned in tens of millions; he built on a princely scale—mound inside the gate, twin market streets, cinnabar hall steps, jade-green door fittings.

sentences.zh: 遊觀射獵，使奴從者被甲持弓弩，陳為步兵；

translations.literal: for pleasure viewing and hunting he had slaves and followers wear armor and hold crossbows, drawn up as foot soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: For hunts and outings he armored retainers with crossbows and drilled them like infantry.

sentences.zh: 止宿離宮，水衡共張，發民治道，百姓苦其役。

translations.literal: he lodged in detached palaces while the superintendent of waters supplied his feasts, conscripted the people to repair roads, and the hundred surnames suffered his corvée.
translations.idiomatic: He slept in detached palaces while the waterworks office catered his feasts and peasants paved his roads—the people groaned under his labor levies.

sentences.zh: 內懷奸邪，欲管朝政，推親近吏主簿張業以為尚書，蔽上壅下，內塞王路，外交籓臣，驕奢僭上，壞亂制度，案根骨肉至親，社稷大臣，先帝棄天下，根不悲哀思慕，山陵未成，公聘取故掖庭女樂五官殷嚴、王飛君等，置酒歌舞，捐忘先帝厚恩，背臣子義。

translations.literal: Inwardly he harbored treachery and wished to manage court government; he promoted his intimate clerk chief registrar Zhang Ye to be master of writing, blocking the sovereign above and damming subordinates below, stopping the kingly path within and befriending feudatory ministers without; arrogant and presumptuous toward the sovereign, he ruined and threw into confusion the institutions-in the case of Gen, though bone and flesh of the closest kin and a minister of the altars of soil and grain, when the former emperor abandoned the realm Gen felt no grief or longing; before the mausoleum mound was finished he publicly took in marriage the former Yeeting musicians of the Five Offices, Yin Yan and Wang Feijun and others, set up wine and song and dance, cast off memory of the former emperor's deep grace, and betrayed the duty of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: In his heart he meant to seize the government, packing the Masters of Reading with his clerk Zhang Ye, blinding you above and choking the bureaucracy below, sealing the royal road within while courting princes without—presumptuous, lawless, a pillar of state who felt no grief when the late emperor died, who wedded Yeeting musicians Yin Yan and Wang Feijun before the imperial tomb was finished, feasted to music, and forgot a subject's debt.

sentences.zh: 及根兄子成都侯況幸得以外親繼父為列侯侍中，不思報厚恩，亦聘取故掖庭貴人以為妻，皆無人臣禮，大不敬不道。

translations.literal: Moreover Gen's elder brother's son Marquis of Chengdu Kuang, favored as affinal kin succeeding his stepfather as full marquis and palace attendant, did not think to repay deep grace but also took in marriage a former Yeeting noble lady as wife-both lacked the ritual of subjects, greatly irreverent and contrary to the Way."
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Kuang of Chengdu, ennobled through a stepfather and serving at court, likewise wedded a cast-off palace lady—utter contempt for a minister's duty."

sentences.zh: 」於是天子曰：「先帝遇根、況父子，至厚也，今乃背忘恩義！

translations.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven said: "The former emperor treated Gen and Kuang, father and son, with the utmost generosity; now they have turned their backs and forgotten kindness and righteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered: "The late sovereign showered Gen and Kuang with favor—how dare they forget it!

sentences.zh: 」以根嘗建社稷之策，遣就國。

translations.literal: " Because Gen had once framed policies for the altars, he was sent to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gen had once set state policy, so he was banished to his fief only.

sentences.zh: 免況為庶人，歸故郡。

translations.literal: Kuang was degraded to commoner and returned to his former commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was stripped to commoner rank and sent home.

sentences.zh: 根及況父商所薦舉為官者，皆罷。

translations.literal: All whom Gen and Kuang's father Shang had recommended for office were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Every man Gen and Kuang's father Shang had placed in office was cashiered.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，傅太后、帝母丁姬皆稱尊號。

translations.literal: Two years later Grand Empress Dowager Fu and the emperor's mother Lady Ding both received exalted titles.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on, Grand Empress Dowager Fu and the emperor's mother Lady Ding received lofty titles.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「新都侯莽前為大司馬，貶抑尊號之議，虧損孝道，及平阿侯仁臧匿趙昭儀親屬，皆就國。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized: "Marquis of Xindu Mang, formerly grand marshal, opposed the discussion of exalted titles and injured filial piety; together with Marquis of Ping'e Ren, who harbored the kin of Zhao the fair lady, let both go to their states."
translations.idiomatic: The ministry reported: "Mang of Xindu, ex-grand marshal, blocked the honor titles and wounded filial duty; Ren of Ping'e hid Zhao the fair lady's kin—both must return to their fiefs."

sentences.zh: 」天下多冤王氏。

translations.literal: The realm for the most part thought the Wangs wrongly treated.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the empire thought the Wangs had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 諫大夫楊宣上封事言：「孝成皇帝深惟宗廟之重，稱述陛下至德以承天序，聖策深遠，恩德至厚。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Yang Xuan submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Emperor Cheng pondered deeply the weight of the ancestral temples and praised Your Majesty's supreme virtue to receive heaven's order; the sage plan was far-reaching and the grace and virtue supremely thick.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandee Yang Xuan sealed a plea: "Emperor Cheng weighed the temples deeply and praised your virtue as heir to heaven; his design was far-sighted, his kindness immense.

sentences.zh: 惟念先帝之意，豈不欲以陛下自代，奉承東宮哉！

translations.literal: Only considering the former emperor's intent, was it not his wish that Your Majesty replace him and serve the Eastern Palace!
translations.idiomatic: Surely the late emperor meant you to take his place and wait on the Eastern Palace!

sentences.zh: 太皇太后春秋七十，數更憂傷，敕令親屬引領以避丁、傅。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager is seventy in years and has repeatedly suffered grief and injury; she has ordered her kin to draw back their necks to avoid the Ding and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager is seventy and heartsore; she has told her kin to shrink back before the Ding and Fu.

sentences.zh: 行道之人為之隕涕，況於陛下，時登高遠望，獨不漸於延陵乎！

translations.literal: Travelers on the road weep for it-how much more Your Majesty, who from time to time climbs high and looks far-does Your Majesty alone feel no shame before Yanling!"
translations.idiomatic: Wayfarers weep at the sight—will you, who mount high towers and gaze afar, feel no shame before Emperor Cheng's Yanling tomb?"

sentences.zh: 」哀帝深感其言，復封商中子邑為成都侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai was deeply moved by his words and again enfeoffed Shang's middle son Yi as marquis of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Ai restored Wang Shang's middle son, Wang Yi, as marquis of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 元壽元年，日蝕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanshou there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshou 1 brought an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 賢良對策多訟新都侯莽者，上於是徵莽及平阿侯仁還京師侍太后。

translations.literal: Many of the worthy and good who answered the policy questions pleaded for Marquis of Xindu Mang; the emperor thereupon summoned Mang and Marquis of Ping'e Ren back to the capital to attend the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Examination candidates clamored for Mang; the emperor recalled Mang and Ren of Ping'e to wait on the dowager.

sentences.zh: 曲陽侯根薨，國除。

translations.literal: Marquis of Quyang Gen died and his state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gen of Quyang died; his marquisate lapsed.

sentences.zh: 明年，哀帝崩，無子，太皇太后以莽為大司馬，與共徵立中山王奉哀帝後，是為平帝。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Ai died without a son; the grand empress dowager made Mang grand marshal and together with him summoned and established the king of Zhongshan to continue Emperor Ai's line-this was Emperor Ping.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Ai died heirless; the grand empress dowager appointed Mang grand marshal, and together they raised the prince of Zhongshan to continue Ai's line—Emperor Ping.

sentences.zh: 帝年九歲，當年被疾，太后臨朝，委政於莽，莽顓威福。

translations.literal: The emperor was nine years old; that year he fell ill; the empress dowager faced the court and entrusted government to Mang, who monopolized favor and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor was nine and fell sick; the grand empress dowager held court and handed power to Wang Mang, who seized every lever of reward and terror.

sentences.zh: 紅陽侯立莽諸父，平阿侯仁素剛直，莽內憚之，令大臣以罪過奏遣立、仁就國。

translations.literal: Marquis of Hongyang Li was Mang's uncle by senior generation; Marquis of Ping'e Ren was by nature blunt and upright; Mang inwardly feared them and ordered great ministers to memorialize their crimes and send Li and Ren to their states.
translations.idiomatic: Li of Hongyang was Mang's senior uncle; Ren of Ping'e was notoriously blunt—Mang feared both and had ministers drum up charges to pack them off to their fiefs.

sentences.zh: 莽日誑耀太后，言輔政致太平，群臣奏請尊莽為安漢公。

translations.literal: Day by day Mang deceived and dazzled the empress dowager, declaring that his regency had brought great peace; the host of officials memorialized asking to honor Mang as Duke Who Pacifies Han.
translations.idiomatic: Daily he flattered the dowager with tales of peace under his hand until the whole bureaucracy begged to dub him Duke Who Pacifies Han.

sentences.zh: 后遂遣使者迫守立、仁令自殺。

translations.literal: The empress dowager thereupon sent agents to besiege Li and Ren and force them to kill themselves.
translations.idiomatic: She then sent men to hem them in at home and drive them to suicide.

sentences.zh: 賜立謚曰荒侯，子柱嗣，仁謚曰刺侯，子術嗣。

translations.literal: Li was given the posthumous title Marquis Huang; his son Zhu succeeded; Ren was titled Marquis Ci; his son Shu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Li was posthumously shamed as Marquis Wasteland, his son Zhu inheriting; Ren was labeled Marquis Thorn, his son Shu succeeding.

sentences.zh: 是歲，元始三年也。

translations.literal: This was the third year of Yuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: That year was Yuanshi 3 (3 CE).

sentences.zh: 明年，莽風群臣奏立莽女為皇后。

translations.literal: The next year Mang prompted the ministers to memorialize establishing Mang's daughter as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Mang stage-managed a plea to crown his own daughter empress.

sentences.zh: 又奏尊莽為宰衡，莽母及兩太子皆封為列侯，語在《莽傳》。

translations.literal: They also memorialized to honor Mang as Regulator-and-Balance; Mang's mother and both sons bearing princely rank were all enfeoffed as full marquises-the account is in Mang's biography.
translations.idiomatic: They further asked to exalt him as Regulator-and-Balance; his mother and two princely sons each got a full marquisate—the full story sits in Mang's biography.

sentences.zh: 莽既外一群臣，令稱已功德，又內媚事旁側長御以下，賂遺以千萬數。

translations.literal: Mang had already silenced the ministers as a bloc, making them praise his merit and virtue, while inwardly he fawned on every senior attendant of the empress dowager's side and below, bribing them to the tune of tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: He had the whole court singing his praises while he stuffed the dowager's women—from chief attendants down—with bribes counted in the millions.

sentences.zh: 白尊太后姊妹君俠為廣恩君，君力為廣惠君，君弟為廣施君，皆食湯沐邑，日夜共譽莽。

translations.literal: He had the empress dowager's sisters Junxia honored as Lady of Broad Grace, Junli as Lady of Broad Kindness, and Junyi as Lady of Broad Bestowal, all receiving bathing-town revenue, praising Mang day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled her sisters—Junxia, Junli, Junyi—as ladies of broad grace, kindness, and bounty, each with a bathing-town stipend, to hymn his virtues night and day.

sentences.zh: 莽又知太后婦人厭居深宮中，莽欲虞樂以市其權，乃令太后四時車駕巡狩四郊，存見孤寡貞婦。

translations.literal: Mang also knew that as a woman the empress dowager wearied of dwelling deep in the palace; wishing to amuse her and buy her favor, he ordered the empress dowager's carriage in the four seasons to tour the four suburbs, visiting widows, orphans, and chaste wives.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing she loathed the cloistered palace, he sent her on seasonal outings to the outskirts to comfort widows, orphans, and virtuous widows—buying her goodwill with spectacle.

sentences.zh: 春幸繭館，率皇后、列侯夫人桑，遵霸水而祓除；

translations.literal: In spring she favored the Silkworm House; leading the empress and full marquises' wives she tended silkworms, then followed the Ba River to perform the lustration;
translations.idiomatic: In spring she visited the Silkworm House, led the empress and marquises' wives in the mulberry rite, then purified the court along the Ba's banks;

sentences.zh: 夏游篽宿、鄠、杜之間；

translations.literal: in summer she roamed between Bisù, Hu, and Du;
translations.idiomatic: in summer she ranged the parks between Bisù, Hu, and Du;

sentences.zh: 秋歷東館，望昆明，集黃山宮；

translations.literal: in autumn she passed the eastern lodges, gazed on Kunming, and gathered at Huangshan Palace;
translations.idiomatic: in autumn she toured the eastern lodges, looked out on Kunming Pool, and halted at Huangshan Palace;

sentences.zh: 冬饗飲飛羽，校獵上蘭，登長平館，臨涇水而覽焉。

translations.literal: in winter she feasted the Yifei archers, conducted a battue at Shanglan, ascended the lodge at Changping, and looked down on the Jing River.
