translations.idiomatic: in winter she feasted the Yifei marksmen, hunted the Shanglan preserve, climbed Changping Lodge, and gazed on the Jing.

sentences.zh: 太后所至屬縣，輒施恩惠，賜民錢、帛、牛、酒，歲以為常。

translations.literal: In every county the empress dowager visited she invariably showed grace, bestowing cash, silk, oxen, and wine on the people, and this became the yearly rule.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever she stopped she scattered coin, cloth, cattle, and wine until it became an annual ritual.

sentences.zh: 太后從容言曰：「我始入太子家時，見於丙殿，至今五六十歲尚頗識之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said at ease: "When I first entered the heir's household I was received in Bing Hall; even now, fifty or sixty years on, I still remember it fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: She mused aloud, "When I first entered the heir's palace I was presented in Bing Hall—fifty or sixty years later I still remember every corner.

sentences.zh: 」莽因曰：「太子宮幸近，可一往遊觀，不足以為勞。

translations.literal: " Mang thereupon said: "The heir's palace lies conveniently near; you could go once on an excursion without its being any labor.
translations.idiomatic: Mang said softly, "The heir's palace is just next door—a short visit would cost you little fatigue.

sentences.zh: 」於是太后幸太子宮，甚說。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the empress dowager favored the heir's palace and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: She made the visit and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 太后旁弄兒病在外舍，莽自親侯之。

translations.literal: A favorite child of the empress dowager's side fell ill in an outer lodge; Mang went in person to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: When a young favorite of hers sickened in an outer lodging, Mang himself attended the sickbed.

sentences.zh: 其欲得太后意如此。

translations.literal: Such was how he sought to win the empress dowager's mind.
translations.idiomatic: That was the lengths to which he went to read her wishes.

sentences.zh: 平帝崩，無子，莽徵宣帝玄孫選最少者廣戚侯子劉嬰，年二歲，托以卜相為最吉。

translations.literal: Emperor Ping died without a son; Mang summoned the great-great-grandsons of Xuandi and chose the youngest, the son of Marquis of Guangqi, Liu Ying, two years old, claiming divination and physiognomy showed him most auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Ping died heirless; Mang called up Xuandi's most remote descendants and fixed on the two-year-old son of the Guangqi marquis, Liu Ying, insisting omens and face-reading marked him the luckiest choice.

sentences.zh: 乃風公卿奏請立嬰為孺子，令宰衡安漢公莽踐祚居攝，如周公傅成王故事。

translations.literal: He then prompted dukes and ministers to memorialize asking to establish Ying as the infant heir and to order Regulator-and-Balance Duke Who Pacifies Han Mang to mount the dais as regent after the precedent of the Duke of Zhou fostering King Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He orchestrated a memorial to make Ying the "infant heir" and set Mang, Duke Who Pacifies Han, on the regent's dais like the Duke of Zhou guiding young Cheng.

sentences.zh: 太后不以為可，力不能禁，於是莽遂為攝皇帝，改元稱制焉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager did not think this right but lacked strength to forbid it; thereupon Mang became regent emperor and changed the era name and proclaimed edicts in his own voice.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager thought it wrong but could not stop it; Mang became regent-emperor, changed the reign title, and issued edicts as sovereign.

sentences.zh: 俄而宗室安眾侯劉崇及東郡太守翟義等惡之，更舉兵欲誅莽。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Chong, marquis of Anzhong in the imperial clan, and Zhai Yi, governor of Dong commandery, and others detested this and in turn raised troops wishing to execute Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon imperial clansman Liu Chong of Anzhong and Zhai Yi of Dong commandery, hating what they saw, rose in arms to kill Mang.

sentences.zh: 太后聞之，曰：「人心不相遠也。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager heard it she said: "The hearts of men are not far from one another.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the news she said, "Men's hearts are not so different from mine.

sentences.zh: 我雖婦人，亦知莽必以是自危，不可。

translations.literal: Though I am a woman, I know Mang must thereby endanger himself-it will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Even I, a woman, know this will only doom Mang—it cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 」其後，莽遂以符命自立為真皇帝，先奉諸符瑞以白太后，太后大驚。

translations.literal: " Afterward Mang thereupon relied on talismanic mandates to set himself up as true emperor; first he presented the various auspicious tokens to inform the empress dowager, and the empress dowager was greatly shocked.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mang used forged portents to declare himself true emperor; he first laid every talisman before the dowager, who reeled in horror.

sentences.zh: 初，漢高祖入咸陽至霸上，秦王子嬰降於軹道，奉上始皇璽。

translations.literal: At first, when Han Gaozu entered Xianyang and reached Bashang, the Qin prince Ying surrendered at Zhidao and offered up the First Emperor's seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bang entered Xianyang and halted at Bashang, the last Qin prince surrendered at Zhidao and handed up the First Emperor's jade seal.

sentences.zh: 及高祖誅項籍，即天子位，因御服其璽，世世傳受，號曰漢傳國璽，以孺子未立，璽臧長樂宮。

translations.literal: When Gaozu executed Xiang Ji and assumed the Son of Heaven's seat, he therefore in imperial dress took the seal; generation after generation received it in succession; it was called the Han heirloom seal of transmission; because the infant heir had not been established, the seal was stored in Changle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After he slew Xiang Yu and took the throne he wore it in court; each reign passed it down as Han's heirloom seal of state; with no infant yet enthroned, it lay in Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 及莽即位，請璽，太后不肯授莽。

translations.literal: When Mang assumed the throne he asked for the seal; the empress dowager was unwilling to give it to Mang.
translations.idiomatic: When Mang seized the throne he demanded the seal; the dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 莽使安陽侯舜諭指。

translations.literal: Mang sent Marquis of Anyang Shun to convey his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Wang Shun of Anyang to argue his case.

sentences.zh: 舜素謹敕，太后雅愛信之。

translations.literal: Shun had always been scrupulous and restrained; the empress dowager had long loved and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was sober and dutiful, and she had long loved and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 舜既見，太后知其為莽求璽，怒罵之曰：「而屬父子宗族蒙漢家力，富貴累世，既無以報，受人孤寄，乘便利時，奪取其國，不復顧恩義。

translations.literal: When Shun appeared, the empress dowager knew he had come for Mang to seek the seal; she angrily reviled him: "You lot-father and son and whole clan-have received Han's strength, riches and honor for generations, yet you have no way to repay it; you took charge of a lone orphan, seized the state when the moment was convenient, and never again looked to kindness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When she saw him she knew why he had come and railed: "Your whole line has fattened on Han for generations, yet you repay a widowed house by stealing the realm when the boy was helpless, with never a thought for grace or duty.

sentences.zh: 人如此者，狗豬不食其餘，天下豈有而兄弟邪！

translations.literal: Men such as this-even dogs and swine would not eat what remains of them; can there be brothers like you in the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Men so vile dogs and pigs would scorn their leavings—are there truly brothers as base as you under heaven?

sentences.zh: 且若自以金匱符命為新皇帝，變更正朔服制，亦當自更作璽，傳之萬世，何用此亡國不詳璽為，而欲求之？！

translations.literal: Moreover if you yourself, trusting the metal casket and talismanic mandate, are the new emperor, changing the first month of the year and court dress, you ought yourself to make a new seal and transmit it for myriad ages-why use this ill-omened seal of a perished state and seek to obtain it?
translations.idiomatic: If your gilded box and forged charts make you emperor, change the calendar and robes yourself and cast a new seal for endless ages—why crave this ill-starred relic of a fallen dynasty?

sentences.zh: 我漢家老寡婦，旦暮且死，欲與此璽俱葬，終不可得！

translations.literal: I am an old widow of the Han house; morning and evening I shall die; I wish to be buried with this seal-yet in the end I cannot!
translations.idiomatic: I am Han's old widow, dying by the day—I mean to take this seal to the grave, and you shall not have it!

sentences.zh: 」太后因涕泣而言，旁側長御以下皆垂涕。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager thereupon wept as she spoke; those at her side, senior attendants and below, all wept.
translations.idiomatic: She wept as she spoke; every woman at her side wept with her.

sentences.zh: 舜亦悲不能自止，良久乃仰謂太后：「臣等已無可言者。

translations.literal: Shun too was grieved beyond controlling himself; after a long while he looked up and said to the empress dowager: "Your servants already have nothing further to say.
translations.idiomatic: Shun wept until he could not master himself, then looked up: "We have said all we can.

sentences.zh: 莽必欲得傳國璽，太后寧能終不與邪！

translations.literal: Mang must obtain the heirloom seal of transmission; can the empress dowager in the end refuse to give it!
translations.idiomatic: Mang will have that seal—can you refuse him forever?

sentences.zh: 」太后聞舜語切，恐莽欲脅之，乃出漢傳國璽，投之地以授舜，曰：「我老已死，如而兄弟，今族滅也！

translations.literal: " When the empress dowager heard Shun's words were urgent, she feared Mang might wish to coerce her; she therefore brought out the Han heirloom seal of transmission, cast it to the ground, and gave it to Shun, saying: "I am old and shall die; with brothers like you, now the clan will be exterminated!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the threat in his voice, she feared worse violence; she produced the seal, dashed it to the floor, and thrust it at him: "I am dying; with kinsmen like you the whole house is doomed!

sentences.zh: 」舜既得傳國璽，奏之，莽大說，乃為太后置酒未央宮漸臺，大縱眾樂。

translations.literal: " When Shun had obtained the heirloom seal of transmission, he memorialized it; Mang was greatly pleased and therefore set wine for the empress dowager on the terraced tower of Weiyang Palace, letting music run riot.
translations.idiomatic: Shun reported the prize; Mang rejoiced and threw a banquet for her on Weiyang's terraced tower, music blaring.

sentences.zh: 莽又欲改太后漢家舊號，易其璽綬，恐不見聽，而莽疏屬王諫欲諂莽，上書言：「皇天廢去漢而命立新室，太皇太后不宜稱尊號，當隨漢廢，以奉天命」。

translations.literal: Mang also wished to change the empress dowager's old Han titles and alter her seal-cords, fearing she would not listen; but Mang's distant kinsman Wang Jian, wishing to flatter Mang, submitted a memorial saying: "High Heaven has cast off Han and commanded the establishment of the New House; the grand empress dowager ought not to bear an exalted title but should follow Han in being abolished, to obey heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Mang meant to strip her old Han titles and seals, yet feared refusal—until a remote cousin, Wang Jian, toadying upward, wrote that heaven had cashiered Han for Xin, so the grand empress dowager must drop her lofty style and fall with Han.

sentences.zh: 莽乃車駕至東宮，親以其書白太后。

translations.literal: Mang thereupon drove his carriage to the Eastern Palace and in person laid the memorial before the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Mang drove to the Eastern Palace and showed her the letter himself.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「此言是也！

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "That statement is correct!
translations.idiomatic: She said coldly, "He speaks the truth.

sentences.zh: 」莽因曰：「此悖德之臣也，罪當誅！

translations.literal: " Mang thereupon said: "This is a minister contrary to virtue; his crime deserves execution!
translations.idiomatic: Mang cut in: "Treasonous words—he must die!

sentences.zh: 」於是冠軍張永獻符命銅璧，文言「太皇太后當為新室文母太皇太后。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Champion Zhang Yong presented a talismanic mandate on a bronze disk; the text read: "The grand empress dowager shall be Mother of Culture, grand empress dowager of the New House."
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhang Yong of Champion offered a bronze talisman reading: "The grand empress dowager shall be Mother of Culture of the New dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」莽乃下詔曰：「予視群公，咸曰『休哉！

translations.literal: Mang thereupon issued an edict: "We have looked on the host of dukes; all say, 'How splendid!
translations.idiomatic: Mang issued an edict: "The lords all cry, 'How glorious!

sentences.zh: 其文字非刻非畫，厥性自然』。

translations.literal: Its graphs are neither carved nor painted; their nature is spontaneous.'
translations.idiomatic: The characters are neither carved nor painted—they seem born of themselves.'

sentences.zh: 予伏念皇天命予為子，更命太皇太后為『新室文母太皇太后』，協於新、故交代之際，信於漢氏。

translations.literal: We have bowed in thought: High Heaven has commanded Us as son and again commanded the grand empress dowager as 'Mother of Culture of the New House,' harmonizing with the juncture of new and old, giving faith to the Han line.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has named me son and renamed her Mother of Culture—fitting the handoff from Han to Xin.

sentences.zh: 哀帝之代，世傳行詔籌，為西王母共具之祥，當為歷代母，昭然著明。

translations.literal: In Aidi's reign the age circulated tallies of edicts as an auspice of the Queen Mother of the West providing feast gear; she was to be mother to successive ages-this was luminously clear.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ai the realm passed edict tallies said to foretell the Queen Mother of the West—sign that a mother of ages would arise.

sentences.zh: 於祗畏天命，敢不欽承！

translations.literal: Therefore in reverent awe of heaven's mandate, how dare We not respectfully receive it!
translations.idiomatic: Who then would dare defy such a command?

sentences.zh: 謹以令月吉日，親率群公諸侯卿士，奉上皇太后璽紱，以當順天心，光於四海焉。

translations.literal: We respectfully on an auspicious day of an auspicious month personally lead dukes, marquises, ministers, and grandees to present the grand empress dowager's seal and ribbon, thereby to accord with heaven's mind and shed light on the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: On an auspicious day I shall lead the nobility to surrender her old seal and cord, answering heaven and dazzling the realm."

sentences.zh: 」太后聽許。

translations.literal: The empress dowager listened and granted assent.
translations.idiomatic: She consented.

sentences.zh: 莽於是鴆殺王諫，而封張永為貢符子。

translations.literal: Mang thereupon poisoned Wang Jian to death and enfeoffed Zhang Yong as viscount of Tribute Tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Mang poisoned Wang Jian and made Zhang Yong viscount of the tribute tally.

sentences.zh: 初，莽為安漢公時，又諂太后，奏尊元帝廟為高宗，太后晏駕後當以禮配食云。

translations.literal: At first, when Mang was Duke Who Pacifies Han, he again flattered the empress dowager by memorializing to honor Yuandi's temple as Gaozong, saying that after the empress dowager's carriage-heaven she would by rite share sacrifice there.
translations.idiomatic: While still Duke Who Pacifies Han he had Yuandi's shrine raised to Gaozong, promising she would share its offerings after her death.

sentences.zh: 及莽改號太后為新室文母，絕之於漢，不令得體元帝。

translations.literal: When Mang changed the empress dowager's title to Mother of Culture of the New House, he cut her off from Han and would not let her share Yuandi's person.
translations.idiomatic: Once she became Mother of Culture of Xin, he severed her from Han and blocked her union with Yuandi in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 墮壞孝元廟，更為文母太后起廟，獨置孝元廟故殿以為文母篹食堂，既成，名曰長壽宮。

translations.literal: He overthrew Xiaoyuan's temple and for Mother of Culture, empress dowager, raised a new temple, alone setting the former hall of Xiaoyuan's temple to be Mother of Culture's refectory for offerings; when finished it was named Longevity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He razed Emperor Yuan's temple, built her a new shrine, and turned Yuan's old hall into a dining hall for her cult, naming the complex Longevity Palace.

sentences.zh: 以太后在，故未謂之廟。

translations.literal: Because the empress dowager was still alive, they did not yet call it a temple.
translations.idiomatic: While she lived they dared not call it a full temple.

sentences.zh: 莽以太后好出遊觀，乃車駕置酒長壽宮，請太后。

translations.literal: Because the empress dowager loved outings and sightseeing, Mang drove his carriage, set wine at Longevity Palace, and invited the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing her love of outings, he laid a feast at Longevity Palace and summoned her.

sentences.zh: 既至，見孝元廟廢徹塗地，太后驚，泣曰：「此漢家宗廟，皆有神靈，與何治而壞之！

translations.literal: When she arrived and saw Xiaoyuan's temple demolished and strewn over the ground, the empress dowager was shocked and weeping said: "This is the Han ancestral temple; all have numinous spirits-by what right do you destroy it!
translations.idiomatic: She arrived to find Yuan's shrine razed to rubble and cried, "These were Han's spirit halls—by what right have you torn them down?

sentences.zh: 且使鬼神無知，又何用廟為！

translations.literal: Moreover, supposing the ghosts lack awareness, why need a temple at all!
translations.idiomatic: If the shades know nothing, why keep a temple?

sentences.zh: 如令有知，我乃人之妃妾，豈宜辱帝之堂以陳饋食哉！

translations.literal: If they have awareness, I am a mere consort of a man-how should I disgrace an emperor's hall by spreading food offerings here!
translations.idiomatic: If they know, I am only a late emperor's concubine—how dare I profane his hall with a banquet!

sentences.zh: 」私謂左右曰：「此人嫚神多矣，能久得晁乎！

translations.literal: She privately said to those at her side: "This man has insulted the spirits too often; how can he long hold the bright mandate (reading 晁 as 朝, the dynasty's fortune)!
translations.idiomatic: She whispered to her women, "He has mocked the spirits once too often—how long can his luck hold before heaven turns?

sentences.zh: 」飲酒不樂而罷。

translations.literal: " They drank wine unhappily and broke off.
translations.idiomatic: The feast ended in gloom.

sentences.zh: 自莽篡位後，知太后怨恨，求所以媚太后無不為，然愈不說。

translations.literal: After Mang usurped the throne, knowing the empress dowager harbored resentment, he sought every way to flatter the empress dowager, yet she grew ever less pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once he seized the throne he tried every blandishment, yet she only grew colder.

sentences.zh: 莽更漢家黑貂，著黃貂，又改漢正朔伏臘日。

translations.literal: Mang changed Han's black sable furs to yellow sable and altered Han's first month and the days of the winter and La festivals.
translations.idiomatic: He swapped Han's black court furs for yellow and moved New Year's day and the La festival.

sentences.zh: 太后令其官屬黑貂，至漢家正臘日，獨與其左右相對飲酒食。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered her officials to wear black sable; on Han's proper La day she alone with those at her side faced one another drinking and eating.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered her staff to keep Han black and, on the old Han La day, drank and dined only with her own attendants.

sentences.zh: 太后年八十四，建國五年二月癸丑崩。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was eighty-four years old; she died on day guichou of the second month of the fifth year of Jianguo.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty-four she died on guichou of the second month, Jianguo 5 (13 CE).

sentences.zh: 三月乙酉，合葬渭陵。

translations.literal: On day yiyou of the third month she was jointly buried at Weiling.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou of the third month she was laid with Emperor Yuan at Weiling.

sentences.zh: 莽詔大夫揚雄作誄曰：「太陰之精，沙麓之靈，作合於漢，配元生成。

translations.literal: Mang ordered grandee Yang Xiong to compose an elegy saying: "Essence of the Great Yin, spirit of Shalu, joined with Han, paired with Yuan to beget Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mang had Yang Xiong compose an elegy: "Essence of the great yin, spirit of Shalu, wed to Han, mate of Yuan who bore Cheng.

sentences.zh: 」著其協於元城沙麓。

translations.literal: " This displayed her concord with Yuancheng and Shalu.
translations.idiomatic: The lines bound her fate to Yuancheng and the Shalu omen.

sentences.zh: 太陰精者，謂夢月也。

translations.literal: By "essence of the Great Yin" is meant the dream of the moon.
translations.idiomatic: "Great yin" alludes to the moon dream of her mother.

sentences.zh: 太后崩後十年，漢兵誅莽。

translations.literal: Ten years after the empress dowager died, Han troops executed Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years after her death Han armies killed Mang.

sentences.zh: 初，紅陽侯立就國南陽，與諸劉結恩，立少子丹為中山太守。

translations.literal: At first, when Marquis of Hongyang Li went to his state in Nanyang, he formed ties of kindness with the various Liu; Li's younger son Dan became governor of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Li of Hongyang, banished to Nanyang, had befriended the Liu clan; his younger son Dan governed Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 世祖初起，丹降，為將軍，戰死。

translations.literal: When Shizu first rose, Dan surrendered and became a general and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu rose, Dan came over as a general and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 上閔之，封丹子泓為武桓侯，至今。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and enfeoffed Dan's son Hong as marquis of Wuhuan down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and enfeoffed Dan's son Hong as marquis of Wuhuan—a line that survives today.

sentences.zh: 司徒掾班彪曰：三代以來，《春秋》所記，王公國君，與其失世，稀不以女寵。

translations.literal: Recorder to the Minister of Education Ban Biao said: Since the Three Ages, what the Spring and Autumn Annals records of kings, dukes, state lords, and their loss of the age rarely does not proceed from favor to women.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Biao, clerk to the minister of education, wrote: Since the Three Dynasties, the Annals show that when kings and lords lost their thrones, a woman's favor was seldom far from the cause.

sentences.zh: 漢興，后妃之家呂、霍、上官，幾危國者數矣。

translations.literal: When Han rose, the households of empresses and consorts-Lü, Huo, and Shangguan-several times nearly brought down the state.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han, the Lü, Huo, and Shangguan consort clans nearly toppled the state more than once.

sentences.zh: 及王莽之興，由孝元后歷漢四世為天下母，饗國六十餘載，群弟世權，更持國柄，五將十侯，卒成新都。

translations.literal: As for Wang Mang's rise, it came through Empress Xiaoyuan, who through four Han reigns was mother of the realm, enjoying the state more than sixty years; her younger brothers held power generation after generation, in turn grasping the state's handle-five generals, ten marquises-until Xindu was finally achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang rose because Empress Xiaoyuan was mother to the realm across four reigns for sixty years; her brothers passed the baton of power—five generals, ten marquises—until Xin was won.

sentences.zh: 位號已移於天下，而元后卷卷猶握一璽，不欲以授莽，婦人之仁，悲夫！

translations.literal: Though titles and ranks had already shifted to all under heaven, Empress Yuan still clutched one seal and was unwilling to give it to Mang-womanly kindness-how pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: The regalia had passed to another house, yet she clung to one jade seal, refusing Mang to the last—womanly softness—how tragic!
